right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based

fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

I have a complete picture now. Here's the report.

## Summary

**Framework:** Next.js 15 (frontend workspace) + NestJS backend + Prisma DB. Content is DB-backed at runtime (`SiteContent` row, fetched via `/api/content`), but **`frontend/data/seed.json` is the source of truth in the repo** — it's what seeds/reseeds the DB (`backend/prisma/seeders/site-content.seeder.ts`, run via `npm run db:seed`). No CLI scaffolding script exists for content (no `new:research` command); there's an admin dashboard at `frontend/app/ad-min` but editing the JSON + reseeding is the code-level path.

**1. Route:** The "Research" tab is not a standalone route — it's a tab inside `/documents` (`frontend/app/documents/page.tsx`). The tab `id` is still `'blogs'` internally (kept for compat) but its **label is "Research"** (line 111: `{ id: 'blogs', label: 'Research', content: <BlogsTab .../> }`). Detail pages render at `/blog-detail?slug=<id-or-slug>`.

**2. Data file:** `frontend/data/seed.json` → `documents.blogs` (a JSON array). Confirmed via the merged branch `content/blog-to-research` (commit `0cb6880`, already on `main`).

**3. Exact schema + real example** (the only current entry, `CmsBlogPost` type in `frontend/lib/types.ts:33-45`):
```json
{
  "id": "eye-of-the-heart",
  "slug": "eye-of-the-heart",
  "extra": "featured",
  "heroType": "type-report",
  "tagClass": "blog",
  "tagLabel": "Ongoing Research",
  "cat": "research",
  "title": "The Eye of the Heart",
  "desc": "Why being heard by another human heals loneliness, isolation, and depression — the convergent science behind HEARD, and the honest gaps our field study is closing.",
  "author": "Said Mohaddes Sadeqi",
  "initials": "SM",
  "role": "Founder & President · Third Eye Worldwide",
  "date": "July 2026",
  "meta": "22 min · Applied research"
}
```
Fields (`CmsItemMeta` base adds `visible`/`order` automatically at seed-normalization time, don't set them manually): `id`, `slug`, `title`, `desc`, `tagLabel`, `author`, `initials`, `role`, `date`, `meta`/`readTime`, plus display-only `extra`, `heroType`, `tagClass`, `cat` (used for the filter pills on the grid).

**4. Important gap for your use case:** `DocCard.tsx` (`frontend/components/documents/DocCard.tsx`) hardcodes every card's link to `/blog-detail` regardless of `id`/`slug` — there is currently only one detail page, and its entire article body (abstract, findings, references, etc.) is **hand-written HTML in `frontend/lib/pages/blog-detail.ts`** (795 lines), not data-driven per entry beyond the byline fields. Adding two new entries that just link out to GitHub repos (`third-eye-kit`, `third-eye-kit-v2`) means either:
   - (a) writing two more full bespoke sections into `blog-detail.ts` (heavy, not warranted for a repo link), or
   - (b) adding a `url` field to the two new `documents.blogs` entries and tweaking `DocCard` to `href={doc.url || '/blog-detail'}` with `target="_blank"` when external — a ~3-line change, reusing the existing card/grid/filter UI as-is.

Given the ladder: (b) is the lazy-correct fix — no new page, no new component, one small conditional in the existing card. Files to touch: `frontend/data/seed.json` (add 2 objects to `documents.blogs`), `frontend/components/documents/DocCard.tsx` (external-link handling), and optionally `frontend/lib/types.ts` (add `url?: string` to `CmsBlogPost`). No slug/naming convention beyond kebab-case `id`/`slug` matching the repo name (e.g. `third-eye-kit`, `third-eye-kit-v2`).
